Enterprise value less market capitalization is therefore not this column and runs above it wherever a listed subsidiary sits inside the group: the two differ by US$13.5bn on Wistron, which consolidates Wiwynn, and by US$28.0bn on Intel. ASE's two lines carry different market capitalizations, US$84,000m on the TWSE line against US$81,063m on the ADR, because the ADR closed 3.5% below the local price that day; each line's multiples are struck on its own price and its own estimate panel. Blank cells have no Bloomberg value: ChipMOS has no BEst EPS panel, Chipbond's price-to-book is empty on both lines, and Unisem's FY2026E P/E is suppressed because the estimate rounds to MYR 0.06, below the precision at which the multiple carries information. Index rows show price performance and index-level P/E only. There is no proxy statement for a foreign private issuer, so no compensation peer group exists to seed the universe.

ASE carries the highest FY2026E P/E and the highest price-to-book of any non-Chinese OSAT in the table, 32.7x and 7.6x. The premium is not on every measure: Unisem's EV/EBITDA exceeds ASE's in all three years, 19.3x, 14.9x and 12.9x against 16.2x, 11.1x and 8.6x, and Unisem's P/E exceeds ASE's in FY2027E and FY2028E, 38.5x and 30.5x against 21.8x and 16.4x. The three Chinese OSATs carry higher FY2026E P/Es (JCET 47.9x, Tongfu 51.5x, Tianshui Huatian 55.7x) on lower earnings bases. Against TSMC, ASE is at a premium on P/E and EV/EBITDA and a discount on P/B. The widest repricing in this universe is the substrate layer the value chain identifies as ASE's structural constraint. Unimicron is +293% year to date at 11.1x book, Nan Ya PCB +295% at 13.2x, Kinsus +354% at 8.5x, with twelve-month FY2027E EPS revisions of +272%, +441% and +259% against ASE's +81%.

17. Forward model summary

This is an operating model, projecting revenue through free cash flow across FY2026E–FY2033E on the audited 20-F basis, tied line by line to FY2025.

Packaging is built as LEAP assembly plus mainstream advanced plus wirebonding plus discrete, where wirebonding is installed bonders times revenue per bonder. Testing is average installed testers times revenue per tester, with net adds treated as a capex decision at the disclosed marginal cost of US$1.05–1.14m per net tester. EMS is modelled as one growth rate because the pass-through and value-added components cannot be separated forward. Segment gross profit is solved from the disclosed ATM gross margin plus a testing-over-packaging spread, because ASE stopped reporting the two separately from the FY2024 20-F. Depreciation is a roll-forward: the prior year's charge less 4.5% of roll-off plus new depreciation on capital placed in service, with capex entering service 45% one year after it is incurred and 20% within the year.

Revenue compounds 7.9% a year to FY2033 and diluted EPS 10.9%. The eight years split into a two-year capacity-constrained boom, a depreciation-absorption year, a digestion year and a normal recovery. Consolidated operating margin peaks at 12.5% in FY2027, 0.4 points above the FY2022 cycle high, then compresses to 7.9% in FY2029 before recovering.

The model's diluted EPS is net income to owners divided by diluted shares, so its FY2025A figure of NT$9.03 sits above the audited 20-F diluted EPS of NT$8.75 shown in §13.1, which also deducts a subsidiary-level dilution adjustment; the gap of about 3% travels through every forward EPS row here and through the consensus comparison in §17.5. The FY2025A ATM gross margin of 23.8% is the audited segment-note computation, not the 23.5% ASE reports on its management basis and that §3.4, §8 and §10.3 use. And free cash flow is operating cash flow less cash capex, which the model runs at 96% of the accrual capex row above, the FY2025 realised ratio of NT$164,643m cash on NT$171,617m accrual; FY2026's NT$332,850m of accrual capex is NT$319,536m of cash.

Bear is the capacity landing into flat demand: LEAP grows +41% in FY2027 against the base's +70%, is flat in FY2028 and declines 20% in FY2029; mainstream advanced growth goes to +3%, 0%, then −10%; wirebond revenue per bonder loses the shortage rent; revenue per tester declines from FY2027 as the fleet added in FY2026–27 runs part-loaded; ATM gross margin retraces to 21.0% by FY2029, which on management's own map is roughly 62% utilization; capex is cut but not below replacement; the NT dollar appreciates to 29.0; and the cost of debt rises to 3.6–3.8% on an 86.9% floating book. Bull is the 2027 doubling happening as guided and the structural range being formally raised: LEAP doubles to US$7.6bn in FY2027, ATM gross margin breaks 30% and holds at 31–32%, tester adds run 1,600–2,100 a year, capex stays at US$9.0–11.5bn, and the payout is trimmed to 60–65% to part-fund the build.

Cumulative FY2026–FY2033 free cash flow is −NT$59,555m in bear on NT$1,559,050m of capex, +NT$171,230m in base on NT$1,687,350m, and −NT$9,311m in bull on NT$2,655,950m. The bull case ends eight years with cumulative free cash flow still negative, because growth here is bought with capital and the faster it grows the longer the cash gap runs.

17.3 Assumptions

Driver Base (FY2027 point) Assessment
atm_gross_margin 29.0% The largest driver in the model. Base FY2026 of 28.8% and FY2027 of 29.0% both exceed ASE's all-time full-year ATM gross margin of 28.7% (FY2022), and FY2028's 28.0% is a third year within 0.7 points of it. Inverting management's published map at 0.4 points per point of utilization, 29.0% implies about 82.5% blended utilization sustained across four quarters, above 2Q26's 80–85% where capacity was already "generally very close to being full," while the tester fleet grows 15% with new lines in tuning. In the reference class, 5 of 126 company-years reached 30% and all five are a pure-play test house. Give-back after an above-trend year has a −2.0-point median at +3, and ASE's own local proof is harsher. Against that, 1H26 realised 26.7%, management guides 28–29% for 3Q26 and above 30% for 4Q26, and ASE beat its ATM gross-margin guide in 19 of 24 quarters; the first three are the company's own forecast rather than independent evidence. Exposure is roughly 1.0–1.5 points, or NT$6–9bn of FY2027 gross profit
capex_usd US$9.0bn Management explicitly refused a FY2027 number, so this is analyst judgment. It assumes a 14% cut from FY2026 against a company that raises the in-year plan every year: FY2026 went US$7.0bn to 8.5bn to 10.5bn in six months, and FY2025 machinery came in 31% above the February plan. The FY2028–29 path of US$7.0bn then US$4.0bn is a 62% cut from the peak, and those cuts produce the FY2030 and FY2031 incremental operating margins of 38.7% and 31.5%, both above anything ASE has achieved. A step-down is precedented, and 29.9% of revenue in FY2027 is still roughly p85 of the class. Largest cash driver in the model at NT$669,497m of cumulative free-cash-flow swing
leap_revenue_usd US$6.3bn (+70%) The base declines management's stated doubling and takes +70%; LEAP's hit rate is three for three and it is the only multi-year number management has ever given. The problem is that the bear case still has +41% growth, so no scenario in the model contains a LEAP stall, while the entire revenue gap to consensus is this one line. There is no backlog, no take-or-pay and no minimum-volume commitment anywhere. LEAP flat at US$3.7bn in FY2027 removes US$2.6bn, NT$81.9bn at the model's NT$31.5 and 8.6% of base revenue, and sits outside the scenario set
rev_per_tester_growth +4.0% The base implies NT$11.72m (FY2026) and NT$12.19m (FY2027), two consecutive all-time records 7.8% and 12.2% above the FY2022 peak while the fleet grows 43.6%. The FY2025 gain of +13.8% is fully explained by the utilization lift alone, so mix and price contributed roughly zero net, and the most recent three quarters of the disclosed series are flat while the fleet grew 13.4%. Against that, 1H26 already annualises to NT$11.22m and LEAP test scales from about 13% to about 40% of testing revenue
wirebond_rev_per_bonder_growth 0.0% The base holds revenue per bonder at NT$5.10m/yr in both FY2026 and FY2027, 0.6% below the all-time peak set in FY2021, a year management described as full or near-full utilization with wire bond above 85%. Wirebond revenue in FY2025 is still 23% below FY2021 in absolute terms and the 20-F's standing regime is price deflation. The 4Q24-to-2Q26 move is real and outside the disclosure's rounding error, and the CFO confirmed pass-through. A −3% to −5% FY2027 is the more defensible central case
ems_revenue_growth +4.0% +4% is the EMS class median. FY2026's +19.8% is, on management's own account, largely memory pass-through; if that slice unwinds, FY2027 EMS revenue declines 9–18% rather than growing 4%, and the model's bear of −6% does not reach the low end. Flexing this driver bear-to-bull moves FY2028 operating income by only NT$53m, so the error lands on revenue and working capital rather than earnings
new_capex_depreciation_rate 14.3% first full year The 62/38 machinery-to-buildings split is the FY2025 actual held flat for eight years; an 80/20 mix from FY2027 would give 17.0%, above the model's own bear of 16.0%. An independent gross-PP&E cross-check puts FY2028 D&A NT$12.6bn above the model's bear. The base rule reproduces FY2024 actual D&A within 3% and FY2025 within 2%, and rolling gross PP&E at ASE's realised 7.3% rate gives FY2029 D&A within 3.4% of the model
other_operating_cash_inflow NT$15,000m/yr A guess on the largest unexplained item on ASE's balance sheet. Other non-current liabilities added NT$53,165m in the six months to 2Q26, NT$37,585m to NT$90,750m; the base takes NT$50,000m for the whole of FY2026, already below that half-year pace, then cuts it 70% on no evidence. If it is customer prepayment tied to the LEAP build it should run at NT$50–65bn a year through FY2028, leaving the model overstating FY2027–28 debt by NT$70–100bn and NT$2.0–2.9bn of annual pre-tax interest
cost_of_debt 2.90% 28bp below the FY2025 realised P&L rate of 3.18% and 57bp below the all-in cash rate of 3.47%, on a book the model takes to NT$553,101m by FY2027. The realised series rose with the debt rather than against it, 86.9% is floating with no meaningful hedge, and NT$131bn matures in 2027 including a US$2,496m floating facility at 4.02%. A 50bp error on FY2028 average debt is NT$3.0bn pre-tax. Base should sit at 3.1–3.3%
tax_rate 19.5% The two prior peak-profit years produced the two highest effective rates in the record, 22.4% (FY2021) and 21.0% (FY2022), because R.O.C. R&D credits are capped at 30% of income tax payable so their proportional benefit shrinks as pre-tax income grows. The base applies 19.5% to FY2027 pre-tax income 35% above the FY2022 level. Materiality: 2.0 points is NT$2.2bn, NT$0.48 per share
dividend_payout 70.0% of prior-year net income to owners The FY2025 dividend was resolved at NT$6.6 on 4,460,302,582 shares, NT$29,438m, which is 73.6% of FY2025 net income to owners. The model's FY2026 dividend line is NT$28,011m, 4.8% below a disclosed number, because it applies the ratio to weighted-average rather than issued shares. Across eight years that understates dividends by roughly NT$21bn and interest by about NT$600m a year by FY2033. The bull case's cut to 60–65% has no precedent
testing_gm_spread 8.5pp over packaging The disclosed FY2016–FY2023 spread ran 9.1 to 16.7 points with a median of 12.7, so the base sits below the minimum of the entire disclosed record. It has arithmetically zero effect on model output because it only splits a fixed gross-profit pool between two segments
nci_share_of_net_income 3.5% The ten-year series has a 4.90% median and the base sits below nine of ten observations, held flat through the downcycle year even though the ratio historically rises when group profit falls. Moving FY2029 to 5.0% removes NT$0.16 per share
other_nonoperating NT$3,000m/yr The realized ten-year series has a NT$4,556m median and the base sits below eight of ten years, with the bear of zero below all ten. The line includes recurring equity-method income and IAS 20 grant releases, not only one-off gains. Error is against the model, roughly NT$0.24 per share
others_growth +5.0% The +5.0% binds from FY2027; the FY2025-to-FY2026 step in the segment row above is +25.7%, from NT$7,952m to NT$9,996m. The model gives Others a flat 1.7% gross margin, producing an FY2027 operating loss of roughly NT$819m against a disclosed FY2025 pre-tax loss of NT$2,516m on smaller revenue. The drag is understated by roughly NT$1.7bn a year, about 1.6% of FY2027 EPS, in every year and every scenario
mainstream_adv_growth +10.0% The line declined 2.5% in FY2024 and its whole +5.3% two-year CAGR is the FY2025 rebound. The base takes +19.5% then +10.0%, the second year 1.9x the realised two-year CAGR. FY2026 is essentially guided, so only FY2027 is exposed; +6–8% is more defensible
discrete_growth +5.0% The line is 17.6% below its FY2021 level and down in four of the last five years, with a six-year CAGR of +2.4%. The base takes +12%, +5%, +4%. A 5-point growth error is about NT$1.3bn of revenue
da_rolloff_rate 95.5% retained The 4.5% annual roll-off implies an average remaining asset life of about 22 years, which cannot coexist with the five-year equipment life in the companion driver, and only 65% of any year's capex ever enters the schedule. The band of ±0.5pp is far too narrow against a 1.5pp change worth NT$10–14bn of FY2033 D&A. The mis-specification does not affect the result inside the horizon and the model should not be extended past FY2033
fx_ntd_usd NT$31.5 The base sits 3.0% stronger-NT than the run-date spot of 32.465 and 0.4 below management's own 3Q26 assumption of 31.9, so it is a headwind assumption. The bull of 32.5 merely equals spot, so FX upside is truncated.
tester_net_adds 1,300 units 1,950 plus 1,300 over two years is +43.6% on a starting fleet of 7,456, against a largest single-year net add of 1,113. A two-year precedent exists (+44.8% across FY2018–19), 1H26 alone added 989, and the capital arithmetic ties across three independent periods
wirebonder_count_change −1.0% FY2020–FY2025 CAGR is −1.20% and the last three years are −1.1%, −1.1%, −1.2%; the 6-K series annualises to about −1.5%. The bull cell of +0.5% is unsupported: the fleet has not grown in any year since FY2022
ems_gross_margin 9.2% Stripping the pass-through, the model's implied gross profit as a percentage of value-added revenue is 41.9% (FY2026) and 43.8% (FY2027) against a ten-year realised range of 42.5–50.2%, so FY2026 is below the ten-year minimum
rd_pct_revenue / sgna_pct_revenue 4.75% each In NT$ the base has R&D growing 22.9% in FY2026, above anything in the record, so the declining ratio is a revenue effect rather than a spending cut. SG&A at 4.74% is the FY2025 actual, mid-range against a ten-year band of 4.46–5.51%. Impairment sits in this line and the model contains no impairment across eight years and three scenarios, which the realised record (NT$127m–NT$992m a year, 0.02–0.21% of revenue, no goodwill impairment even at 60% utilization in FY2023) supports
diluted_share_growth / dso_days / dpo_days +1.0% / 70 days / 60 days Share growth is 25bp above the nine-year mean, which is conservative given a 3.64% option overhang and no buyback. DSO sits within one day of the most recent full year; DPO is one day below it, which leaves an unmodelled cash cushion
dio_days 46 days The base equals the FY2025 actual, but the latest quarter is 52.0 days, 13% higher, for the reason the model assumes persists: the EMS component build ahead of the memory price move. Six days is NT$12.1bn of additional working capital in a year when free cash flow is already −NT$73bn. 48–50 days for FY2026–27 is more defensible
leap_assembly_share 75% of LEAP in packaging Evidence covers two years only, and the driver is held identical in bear, base and bull for all eight years, asserting zero uncertainty on a line worth NT$9,922m of FY2027 packaging revenue per 5-point shift. The model's own bull case contradicts a constant split, since it moves the test attach ratio toward 30% of ATM revenue

Currency never touches gross margin in this model. Applied to the FY2028 base ATM revenue of NT$674,417m, 4.2 points of constant-currency gross margin is NT$28,326m, 23% of FY2028 base operating income and the same size class as the largest driver in the table below. Currency enters only as a translation rate on LEAP revenue and capex and does not appear among the sensitivity drivers at all. Management's own rule of thumb is 0.4 points of holding-company gross margin per 1% of NT dollar appreciation, and management quantified a 4.2-point constant-currency gross-margin difference for 3Q25 against 1Q25. The two channels compound: a stronger NT dollar cuts the NT$ translation of US$-denominated LEAP revenue and compresses gross margin at the same time, so the bear FX case is understated on both lines.

1 ATM gross margin NT$57,325m NT$55,905m NT$309,216m

Each row flexes one driver from its bear vector to its bull vector and holds every other driver at base. Against FY2025 operating income of NT$51,421m, a plausible move in ATM gross margin alone is worth more than the entire FY2025 operating result. The capex driver has no direct effect on operating income and the largest effect on everything else, moving cumulative free cash flow by about NT$669bn and peak debt by roughly NT$300bn; about NT$163bn of that swing is the D&A tax shield on the capex itself. ASE has never disclosed the depreciable life of test equipment, and the model runs no separate sensitivity on it. The EMS revenue driver barely moves operating income at all, NT$53m at FY2028, and moves cumulative free cash flow by −NT$36,873m, because faster EMS growth consumes working capital at a 2.4–2.9% operating margin.

FY2026 revenue is within 0.6%; the EPS gap of NT$2.40 sits mostly below the operating line. NT$1.17 is net non-operating income the consensus estimate line implies but the model does not include, NT$0.65 is operating income, NT$0.30 is tax at the FY2025 realised rate rather than the roughly 18% consensus implies, NT$0.13 is a higher share count, and NT$0.15 is unattributed. For FY2027 and FY2028 the largest single component of the revenue gap is LEAP: consensus embeds management's stated doubling and the base takes +70% then +25%, worth roughly NT$34,650m of the NT$95,411m FY2027 gap and NT$85,000m of the NT$202,096m FY2028 gap, 36% and 42% of each. The rest is the 30% ATM gross-margin question.

17.6 Modelling conclusions

  • The forecast is a capital-intensity question before it is a demand question. Cumulative FY2026–FY2033 capex of NT$1,687,350m produces a revenue gain of NT$543,425m, 0.32 of incremental revenue per unit of capex, below the OSAT class median of 0.37 and less than half ASE's own historical 0.78. Even the FY2026–FY2028 window, where the revenue is guided, converts at 0.45.
  • Depreciation rather than demand produces the FY2028 compression. FY2028 revenue grows 7.8% and operating income 5.3%, an 8.5% incremental margin, while D&A rises NT$19,569m in that year alone. The compression is depreciation, not demand.
  • The next downcycle costs more than the last one. Base FY2029 shows a 69.4% decremental against the 44.4% ASE realised in FY2023, because the fixed base is 2.4x larger. In bear, FY2029 operating margin falls to 3.8% on a 10.8% revenue decline.
  • Free cash flow does not turn positive until FY2028 in base and never turns cumulatively positive in bull. ASE has been free-cash-flow negative in five of the last six quarters, 4Q25 excepted, and the model adds two to three more years. Debt peaks between NT$611,864m (base) and NT$917,432m (bull) against NT$261,442m at FY2025.
  • The dividend is the one line that does not flex. At 70% of the prior year's earnings the base pays NT$28,011m to NT$61,483m a year through the negative free-cash-flow window, NT$409,842m cumulatively, funded from borrowing in three of the eight years. Nothing in the record suggests the board trims it.

18. Risks

Risk 1 — AI capex is being installed ahead of the revenue, debt-funded, into a fixed-cost base that cannot be unwound. Mechanism: ASE's testing operations and leading-edge packaging are, in its own words, "characterized by relatively high fixed costs." It is installing that capacity faster than operating cash flow funds it and financing the gap with borrowing. The resulting depreciation lands whether or not the demand persists. Exposure: capex to operating cash flow went 47% (FY2023), 88% (FY2024), 116% (FY2025), 149% (1H26). Debt rose NT$40,900m in 2Q26 alone and PP&E rose 12.7% in that quarter. NT$114,686m of contracted equipment purchases sits unpaid, and D&A is already at an NT$80,000m annualised run-rate against NT$67,440m for all of FY2025. Base rate: the FY2023 decremental of 44.4% applied to the 2Q26 annualised revenue base removes roughly NT$45,000m of operating profit on a repeat 13.3% decline, more than half of current operating profit, before incremental depreciation. Leading indicators: blended utilization falling back below 75%; tester count flattening while testing capex stays elevated; net debt to equity through 0.55; capital purchase commitments shrinking sharply, which would signal cancellation; "depreciation rising faster than revenues" recurring in a quarter without revenue growth.

Risk 2 — One unnamed customer is 25.0% of group revenue, and the disclosure was just weakened. Exposure: NT$161,282,046 thousand of FY2025 revenue spanning packaging and EMS; losing a quarter of it removes about NT$40,300m of revenue and NT$17,900m of operating profit at the FY2023 decremental. EMS-basis top-five is 58% against ATM's 44%, so the more concentrated business is the one already shrinking. The delta: FY2025 removed both concentration sentences from the risk factor, the only material quantification deleted without replacement, in the year the single-customer figure reached 25.0%. Amkor names Apple at 29.8% and Qualcomm at 11.1%. Leading indicators: the Note 41(c) amount as a percentage of revenue; the ATM-versus-EMS top-five split each quarter; IDM share of ATM revenue.

Risk 3 — The leading-edge growth line sits on a boundary the foundry partner controls. Exposure: ATM was 66% of 2Q26 revenue and 94% of operating profit, up from 61% and 87% a year earlier, and management attributes the widening gap to LEAP. An adverse re-allocation therefore lands on the highest-margin, highest-capex part of the business, the same part Risk 1's capex is built for. Testing capex alone was US$804m in 2Q26, essentially matched to packaging's US$840m on a segment that is 13% of revenue. Leading indicators: LEAP guidance revisions on the quarterly call, the only place the number is disclosed; the bumping/flip-chip/WLP/SiP share of ATM revenue; testing as a share of ATM revenue; any quarter where testing capex stays elevated while the tester count flattens.

Risk 4 — Utilization is the disclosed margin driver and is never disclosed, and the headroom is nearly gone. Mechanism: fourteen mentions of "capacity utilization rate" in the FY2025 20-F and zero numbers, against a risk factor stating that "unit cost generally decreases as fixed costs are spread over a larger number of units." Exposure: the whole FY2025-to-2026 margin recovery is attributed by management to utilization plus LEAP mix with FX as the offset, and only one of the three appears in any filing. At 80–85% now, with 4Q26 ATM gross margin guided above a 30% ceiling that management's own map puts at full utilization, further margin has to come from price or mix. Leading indicator: one sentence in the prepared remarks of each quarterly call. There is no filing-based substitute.

Risk 5 — Taiwan concentration increased in the year the diversification story was loudest. Exposure: Taiwan generated 58.9% of FY2025 operating revenues, up from 55.1% and 55.4%, and the highest since FY2022, with 67,870 of the 114,179 employees on the 2Q26 headcount there. The FY2025 filing dropped the nuclear-phase-out framing for "increasingly strict energy management measures which could increase our manufacturing costs," an open-ended cost risk. A January 2025 earthquake in southern Taiwan already caused "delay in upstream component availability." Contradiction with the strategy: "given the dynamics of the tariff as well as the exchange rate we have to rethink priority… instead of going to multiple places. We will focus on 1 or 2 overseas areas." The overseas programme was narrowed to one or two areas.

Risk 6 — Refinancing concentration in 2027–2028 into a business that will still be free-cash-flow negative. Exposure: 66% of long-term debt service falls in the one-to-three-year bucket, NT$155,178m including interest, against the NT$149,366m of 2027 and 2028 principal in §12.2's maturity table; the residual 2027 wall after the January conversion and first-quarter early settlements is NT$93bn–NT$131bn, roughly NT$112bn at the midpoint [estimate]; the 100bp sensitivity is NT$1,833m, 3.6% of FY2025 pre-tax profit. Also: PP&E pledged as collateral went from NT$913 thousand to NT$34,209m in one year without a matching increase in disclosed secured borrowings, so unsecured creditors' position deteriorated without a disclosure event.

Risk 7 — EMS is 34% of revenue, 6% of operating profit, and cannot pass costs through within the quarter. Exposure: 2Q26 gross margin 8.9% against 9.5% in 1Q26, operating margin 2.4% against 3.0%, raw materials 79% of revenue. Management attributes the decline principally to product mix, with a higher component-cost environment also named. Segment capex is 2.3% of revenue, so there is no asset-side option value, and EMS carries NT$3,655m of the group's NT$52,542m of goodwill, so NT$48,871m of it is exposed to ATM cash flows.

Risk 8 — Substrate and ABF supply from a supplier base that narrowed while self-supply stayed under 9%. Exposure: 8.7% self-supply by value with internal operations not expected to meet requirements "for the foreseeable future"; the named external supplier base narrowed from five firms in FY2022–23 to three Taiwanese firms in FY2024–25, with LG Innotek, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Toppan dropped. What limits it: management's own statement of where the constraint applies today names equipment installation and building construction, not substrate. Leading indicators: the self-supply percentage in each 20-F; any fourth or fifth name returning to the supplier list; ABF language changing from "may face" to "has faced."

Risk 9 — 93% of group goodwill sits in the two segments taking the capex. Exposure: NT$35,431m allocated to packaging and NT$13,440m to testing, NT$48,871m of the group's NT$52,542m, against FY2025 operating profit of NT$51,421m, so it is roughly 1.0x a year of operating income. The value-in-use test uses five-year management cash-flow projections discounted at pre-tax rates of 11.96%–13.81%, and those projections now embed a LEAP ramp with no disclosed track record. The 20-F states its own trigger logic: "an impairment charge is more likely to occur during a period in which our operating results and outlook are otherwise already depressed." Against that, no goodwill impairment was taken even in FY2023 when utilization went to "slightly above 60%," and that year's total impairment of NT$147m was the second smallest in eight years. Leading indicators: the discount-rate range widening or its top moving above roughly 14%; the sensitivity-analysis wording changing; any impairment in the packaging or testing units specifically.

Risk 10 — Governance and key-person concentration. Exposure: four principals aged 66 to 81, all in place since April 2018, no disclosed succession plan, no mandatory retirement age and no chairman/CEO separation policy. The 20-F states ASE is "not insured against the loss of service of any of our personnel." The COO has been the subject of a criminal proceeding running since 2017 arising from the SPIL tender offers; the FY2025 status is a Supreme Court reversal of the guilty portion on 2025-07-10, an affirmation of the original not-guilty judgment on 2026-02-11, and a further prosecution appeal on 2026-03-02. Related-party real-estate purchases of NT$9,494m across 2024–25 sit inside a segment that lost NT$2,516m pre-tax. ASE also has ongoing environmental proceedings from wastewater-discharge incidents that produced "monetary fines as well as sanctions, including orders to suspend or limit our operations and criminal charges against us," with no amount given.

Risk 11 — Tariffs and trade policy. Exposure: the FY2025 20-F expanded trade policy from two sentences to eight, naming "semiconductor-specific tariffs, which the U.S. government intends to increase over time" and warning that "the imposition of such tariffs could increase our costs, which we may not be able to pass on to our customers." Customers by headquarters are 56.7% US while 58.9% of revenue is produced in Taiwan. Management states it cannot size the pull-forward: "we are unable to quantify such impact as we do not have a method to ascertain inventory build levels from regular order flow." Leading indicator: any quarter where second- or third-quarter revenue undershoots after a strong first half.

Risk 12 — Currency. Exposure: revenues and capex are predominantly USD, costs predominantly NT dollar, RMB, JPY, KRW and EUR. Management's own quarterly attributions: FX cost 1.4 points sequentially and 2.4 points annually of gross margin in 3Q25, with constant-currency 3Q25 gross margin "roughly 4.2 percentage points higher" than 1Q25. FY2024 saw a NT$5,538m net FX loss. The FY2025 20-F removed the three-year FX loss history from the risk factor and substituted a generality. The forward model does not include currency on the margin channel at all.

Which risks arrive together. ASE has written the first of the three sequences below into its own filings across four separate risk factors without connecting them.

  • The AI demand-gap sequence (Risks 1, 3, 4, 9). AI order rates soften, LEAP loading falls, blended utilization drops below the 70% structural-margin threshold, the depreciation from FY2025–27 capex is already in the cost base and cannot be removed, gross margin compresses at the 44.4% decremental, the operating outlook is revised down, and the goodwill value-in-use test then runs on a cut five-year forecast at a 12–14% discount rate.
  • Funding tightens when it is most needed (Risks 1, 6). The same demand softening reduces operating cash flow while NT$155,178m of long-term debt service falls due in 2027–2028 and NT$114,686m of contracted equipment purchases remains unpaid. The equipment commitments cannot be cancelled quickly, and refinancing would happen into weaker credit metrics with NT$34.2bn of PP&E already pledged.
  • The geographic and customer coincidence (Risks 2, 5, 11). A Taiwan disruption, a tariff step and a single-customer product miss all land on the same 58.9%-Taiwan, 25.0%-one-customer revenue base, and they are not independent: a tariff regime penalising Taiwan-origin content gives the largest customer a reason to qualify non-Taiwan capacity, and ASE has just narrowed its overseas expansion to one or two areas.

The historical analogue for the first cluster is FY2022 to FY2023, when a 13.3% revenue decline produced a 48.7% operating-profit decline; §17.6 puts the FY2029 fixed base at 2.4x that level.

Peer evidence: Amkor is running the same play: long-term debt went from US$1,283m (2025-12-31) to US$2,335m (2026-06-30) and capital-expenditure payable from US$243.5m to US$621.3m over the same six months, on capex of US$688.4m in 1H26 against US$226.1m in 1H25, "primarily focused on investments in advanced packaging and test equipment and the Arizona Facility." Both OSATs are debt-funding AI capacity at the same time.

19. Source disclosure

Sources. Ten Form 20-F filings (FY2016–FY2025), eight Form 6-K filings (2024-Q3 through 2026-Q2), 24 earnings-call transcripts (Q3 2020 – Q2 2026), one presentation transcript (a UBS Greater China semiconductor fireside dated 2025-12-03) and six quarterly earnings decks rendering to 94 slides. Peer filings were read for Amkor, TSMC, ChipMOS, Teradyne, Jabil, Flex, Celestica and Sanmina. SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 0001122411, ifrs-full namespace, TWD, FY2015–FY2025 annual frames only) supplied the consolidated spine. A live Bloomberg terminal supplied all price, consensus, peer-history and credit data.

Gaps and failures:

  • Bloomberg was recorded unavailable in Phase 0 and that was wrong. ASX and 3711 are absent from the hardcoded script universe, but the terminal answers 3711 TT Equity, ASX US Equity, 6239 TT, 2449 TT, 8150 TT, 600584 CH, 002156 CH and 002185 CH directly. The six non-SEC OSAT peers in §4 are sourced from aggregators and trade press, not the terminal, even though primary-grade series were available.
  • The second 6-K family was never pulled. ASE furnishes two 6-K families per quarter: the earnings press release or deck, and separately the auditor-reviewed interim consolidated financial statements two to three months later. Zero of the latter were pulled for any quarter, which is why quarterly segment gross margin stops at 4Q25 and 1Q26 and 2Q26 segment economics exist only on the ATM/EMS management basis that does not reconcile to the audited segments.
  • No external dataset was pulled. No figure in this dossier is sourced from one and no [data:] citation appears anywhere.
  • The ten-year spine has no independent third-party cross-check against the discrepancies logged below.
  • No sell-side note text exists. The local digest returns zero hits for ASX, ASE and 3711. Per-analyst reasoning in §14 is reconstructed from the covering analysts' own questions on the earnings calls and from Bloomberg's rating and target roster, which is weaker than reading the notes.
  • No proxy statement and no insider transaction record. As a foreign private issuer ASE files no DEF 14A and its insiders file no Forms 3, 4 or 5. Executive compensation is 20-F Item 6 as a single aggregate; individual bands exist only in the R.O.C. annual report, of which only the FY2024 edition was obtained (the FY2025 edition returns HTTP 403 to automated fetching). Monthly TWSE insider shareholding reports were not pulled. The dossier therefore holds point-in-time ownership and no transaction evidence of any kind.
  • The risk-factor year-over-year comparison in §8 and §18 was built by diffing the Item 3.D sections of ten archived 20-Fs at sentence granularity, not from a pre-built redline.
  • Pre-2020 transcripts. BamSEC holds 72 ASE transcripts back to Q2 2006; 24 were collected, starting at Q3 2020. The SPIL acquisition and its integration therefore have no contemporaneous management commentary.

Discrepancy log: seventeen disagreements were found across the three reconciled sources and all but one were resolved. The material ones: FY2025 net income to owners is NT$40,015.8m under IASB IFRS and NT$40,658m under Taiwan-IFRS, a 1.6% gap that widens to 11.8% for FY2023 and persists in the FY2025 20-F's own comparative column, most likely from the Hirschmann purchase-price allocation applied retrospectively in the unaudited series and not in the audited one; the annual series here uses the 20-F and the quarterly series uses the 6-K, and the two are never summed. FY2025 capex is NT$164,642.5m on a cash basis, NT$171,616.5m on an accrual basis and NT$162,149m as the sum of four quarterly "net payments," and all three reconcile. 1Q26 was restated in the 2Q26 release, so prior quarters are taken from the most recent release throughout. The 20-F and 6-K tester counts are on different as-of dates (January 31 against quarter-end) and are never spliced. Two revenue-mix denominators with near-identical labels exist and are never charted together: 59.6% is a percentage of packaging revenue, 49% is a percentage of ATM revenue. One is unresolved: ATM-basis 1Q25 revenue is NT$86,668m in the 2025-Q1 and 2025-Q2 decks and NT$88,668m in the 2026-Q1 6-K, a NT$2,000m difference with no restatement note, while consolidated 1Q25 revenue is unchanged; the quarterly series uses the later figure.

Internal conflicts this document cannot settle. Six quantities have two defensible bases.

  • ATM gross margin runs on two series 0.3–0.5 points apart. Computed from the audited segment note, ATM gross margin was 28.7% (FY2022), 22.2% (FY2023), 22.9% (FY2024) and 23.8% (FY2025). On the management/6-K basis ASE reports, the same years are 28.5%, 21.8%, 22.5% and 23.5%. §3.4, §4.2, §8, §9 and §10.3 use the management basis because that is the number management is judged against; §14, §17.1 and §17.3 use the computed basis because the consensus and base-rate comparisons are built on segment data.
  • Total debt and net debt differ between §12.5 and §13.1 in every year of the record, by NT$11,188m (FY2020), NT$11,498m (FY2021), NT$12,205m (FY2022), NT$15,304m (FY2023), NT$12,456m (FY2024) and NT$11,503m (FY2025). §12 builds the stack from the FY2025 20-F debt footnote and reaches NT$272,945m of interest-bearing debt, NT$180,476m net and 1.52x net debt to EBITDA. §13.1 and §17.1 take the XBRL spine and reach NT$261,442m, NT$168,973m net and 1.42x. The gap is roughly the NT$8,848m of IFRS 16 lease liabilities plus NT$2,655m the two builds classify differently; nothing in the filings read this run identifies the residual. §10.4's "gross debt" column is a third definition and states its exclusion.
  • Consolidated FY2025 ROIC is 8.2% on the average-invested-capital definition stated in §3.4 and used in §13.1, and 7.7% on the year-end XBRL variant §14 carries forward to its 15.8% FY2027 figure. The §14 pairing is internally consistent; the level should not be compared with §13.1's row.
  • Realized incremental operating margins have been put on the audited §13.1 basis throughout. The alternative Bloomberg/Taiwan-IFRS operating-income series gives FY2020 17.8%, FY2021 29.3%, FY2022 17.9%, FY2024 −8.6%, FY2025 23.2% and an FY2023 decremental of 44.8%, within about a point of the audited figure in each year. The consensus-implied incrementals in §14 for FY2027 and FY2028 reconcile to §13.1 exactly; the FY2026 figure of 24.8% is 0.3 points above what §13.1's own columns produce, because it uses the Bloomberg FY2025 base.
  • The residual 2027 maturity wall is NT$112bn in §12.2 and §18 and NT$131bn in §17.3. The first nets both the January 2026 convertible conversion and about half the first-quarter early settlements; the second nets only the conversion. Neither is disclosed by ASE, and the disclosed range is NT$93bn–NT$131bn.
  • The December 2021 China disposal is "six sites" in §9 and "four China sites" in the §11 ledger, above a five-name list of the entities transferred. The transaction documents distinguish the holding company from the plants beneath it and the archived 20-Fs do not reconcile the count; the consideration, the gain and the unpaid 28.5% are consistent everywhere and are the figures that carry the argument.

Three smaller basis notes. US dollar conversions in this dossier use NT$31.4–31.5 for FY2025 quantities and the 2026-08-03 spot of NT$32.465 for market data, so US dollar figures drawn from different sections differ by up to 3%; §3.4's capex-intensity column is cash capex for the consolidated row and segment-asset expenditures for the segment rows; and §16's Bloomberg enterprise value for ASE is NT$19.5bn below the front matter's, which nets cash plus current financial assets against interest-bearing debt on the definition stated there. The ADR close on 2026-08-03 is US$36.29 in §15's price series and US$36.27 in §16's separate Bloomberg comp pull.

By count: trendforce.com (7), digitimes.com (5), stockanalysis.com (5), taipeitimes.com (3), finance.biggo.com (3), tradingview.com (2), plus single citations from epoch.ai, marklapedus.substack.com, aseglobal.com, mordorintelligence.com, datacenterdynamics.com, yolegroup.com, evertiq.com, semi.org, wsts.org, marketscreener.com, prnewswire.com, analog.com, honhai.com, taiwannews.com.tw, sina.com.cn, investing.com, footnotebrief.com, siliconanalysts.com, usagold.com, jpmorgan.com, semiconductorforu.com, seekingalpha.com, chiplet-marketplace.com, eu.36kr.com and media-aseholdco.todayir.com.

One was contradicted and revised in full, the assertion that foundry encroachment was newly promoted into the FY2025 risk factors, which is present verbatim from FY2021; 42 were narrowed to what the evidence supports. 20. What we still don't know, and the monitoring KPIs

20.1 Unresolved material gaps

  1. Currency is unmodelled on the margin channel and unranked in the sensitivity table. The forward model applies the exchange rate only as a translation on LEAP revenue and capex, never to gross margin, and FX does not appear among the five ranked drivers, even though 4.2 points of constant-currency gross margin on the model's FY2028 ATM revenue base is NT$28,326m, 23% of FY2028 base operating income, against NT$57,325m for the top-ranked driver.
  2. The customer that is 25.0% of revenue is unidentified, and the ten-year series that would constrain it is unread. The amount is disclosed in every 20-F and only FY2023–FY2025 were extracted. The ten-year path would show whether this is a long-standing consumer relationship in decline or a growing one, which determines whether the AI growth is incremental to the largest account or replacing an account that declined 7.6% in FY2025.
  3. No industry-wide advanced-packaging capacity-versus-demand balance exists here. Nothing in this dossier sets the aggregate capacity-addition schedule across ASE, Amkor, SPIL, JCET, Tongfu, Powertech and TSMC's own CoWoS expansion against a unit forecast for AI accelerators. ATM gross margin is the model's number-one driver and in this business ATM gross margin is utilization, so whether 2027–28 is a shortage or a surplus determines the entire margin path. The run answers it only from ASE's own order-book commentary.
  4. The auditor-reviewed interim 6-K financial statements were never pulled, so 1Q26 and 2Q26 segment economics rest on a management basis that does not reconcile to the audited segments. The AI-packaging case turns on packaging-versus-testing economics in those two quarters.
  5. The utilization-to-margin map is quoted as invariant on an asset base whose depreciation grows 93% by FY2028. Management's 70%-to-24% and 85%-to-30% mapping was given once, at the UBS fireside on 2025-12-03, against the asset base as it stood in late 2025. Depreciation as a share of revenue rises across the forecast, which mechanically lowers the gross margin achievable at any given utilization. On the FY2028 asset base the map is not recomputed anywhere, and the bear case assumes it moves without establishing by how much.
  6. Peer financials for the six non-SEC OSAT competitors rest on aggregators, though the Bloomberg terminal served them.
  7. EMS demand, 39.9% of revenue, has no durable-versus-cyclical decomposition. The secular analysis ran once at consolidated level and is ATM-dominated. Whether the communications and automotive weakness is cyclical or structural is not established, and it is the weakest-supported revenue line in the forward model through 2033.
  8. The in-house substrate business is unsized. ASE's own answer to the constraint this dossier calls structural has no disclosed revenue, capex, capacity or margin, and the model assumes "Others" grows with a self-supply effort that has been shrinking for a decade.
  9. No insider transaction evidence of any kind exists, for a company where the chairman is 81, the vice chairman 79, all four senior officers have been in place since April 2018 and no succession plan is disclosed.
  10. Appendix C has no data in it. The one identified external dataset was never fetched.
  11. No country-level capacity, net PP&E, capex or headcount is established, and no analysis of what the absence of a leading-edge US site costs against Amkor's Arizona plant, in the year US semiconductor-specific tariffs entered the risk factors unquantified.
  12. Testing has no attributable demand base. Its customer concentration and end-market split are undisclosed and were not triangulated from the LEAP test share, the ATM top-five series or the ChipMOS and King Yuan disclosures, for the segment taking 40% of the largest capex programme in company history.

20.2 Open questions the disclosure does not answer

  • What gross margin does LEAP actually earn? Management calls it accretive and has never quantified it, and the model treats the whole ATM gross margin as one driver because the split cannot be built at any tier.
  • What share of the tester fleet is customer-consigned or leased rather than owned? The 20-F confirms both practices and quantifies neither, so the true capital intensity of Testing and every return figure for it are bounded rather than known.
  • What is inside "other non-current liabilities," the line that grew NT$30,528m in FY2025 and is now larger than the entire bond stack? Customer prepayment and government grants have opposite implications for the durability of the revenue.
  • What is the depreciable life of LEAP equipment and of testers? The model runs no sensitivity on it; the D&A tax shield inside its capex sensitivity is worth about NT$163bn of cumulative free cash flow.
  • What is the FY2027 capex number? Management refused it on the 2Q26 call and it is the second-largest driver in the model.
  • Is any of the FY2026–FY2027 capacity contracted? No backlog, take-or-pay or minimum-volume commitment is disclosed anywhere.
  • Why did packaging raw-material intensity stay flat while the advanced mix rose 8.3 points, against an industry expectation that advanced packaging costs more in materials? Specifically, does the on-substrate service run on customer- or foundry-supplied substrate the way wafers already arrive on consignment?
  • What secures the NT$34,209m of newly pledged PP&E, given that disclosed secured borrowings are NT$7,972m?
  • What are the actual financial-ratio covenants at the subsidiary borrowers, and what is the headroom? No metric, threshold or level is published anywhere.
  • What did ASE pay for EugenLight, and what does it own? Control was obtained in January 2026 with no consideration, purchase-price allocation or revenue disclosed.
  • What is Hongkong United Ascend Holdings, and what is ASE's 16.48% stake worth? The filings give no Level 3 valuation inputs and do not name the entity's business.
  • Does ASE have any hybrid-bonding programme? The phrase appears nowhere in the FY2023–FY2025 20-Fs or in 24 earnings calls, while Amkor names one.
  • How much of 1H25 and 1H26 revenue was tariff pull-forward? Management states it cannot determine this.

Appendix A — Investor-presentation insights and key slides

The deck corpus is six quarterly earnings-release decks, 94 rendered slides, spanning 2021 to 2026. There is no investor day deck, no capital-markets day, no strategy deck and no product roadmap deck and no investor day; the quarterly investor conference is the earnings call. Almost every word on the strategy and recap slides is read verbatim into the transcript, and the transcripts routinely contain more than the slides: the FY2026 capex split, the count of construction projects and the utilization figure are all spoken and appear on no slide. The additive content is therefore data-shaped rather than strategic.

  • The quarterly mix series exists only on these slides. The archived 6-K set starts at 2024-Q3 and the 20-F reports the type mix annually on a different denominator, so three chart slides are the only local source for the full quarterly path of ATM revenue by service type, 1Q20 to 2Q26. Wirebonding share peaked at 42% of ATM revenue in 2Q21 and is 24% in 2Q26, eighteen points lost in five years while the wirebonder fleet was roughly flat, so the mix shift is growth elsewhere rather than wirebond contraction. The 2020–21 direction was the opposite of the 2022–26 direction, which the archived 6-K series, starting in 2024, does not show. And testing share was flat at 15–18% for four years and only broke out in 4Q24.
  • The capex chart understates capital intensity by about a third. Every deck since 2021 includes a slide titled "Equipment Capital Expenditures vs. EBITDA." The bars are equipment only; buildings, facilities and automation appear nowhere on the chart, its axis or a footnote. Excluded share: 32% (1H2025), 38% (FY2025), 34% (1H2026), 38% (the FY2026 plan). Corrected, 2Q26 total capex was about 1.6x EBITDA rather than the 1.17x the chart shows.
  • The guidance format was downgraded and the decks date the change. The 2021 deck guides ATM in volume and price: "In USD terms, ATM 3rd quarter 2021 volume to increase 12% with ASP holding stable." That is the only quantified volume figure and the only ASP statement anywhere in the local corpus. By 2023 the outlook slide is gone entirely and guidance is revenue-shaped; the 2025 and 2026 decks never restored it. The window closed between mid-2021 and mid-2023.
  • The deck went silent in the downcycle. The 2Q23 deck has thirteen slides and not one word of business commentary: safe harbour, then straight into the profit and loss account, with no outlook slide. The 2Q23 call still contained prepared remarks and forward guidance, so the omission is a deck choice. That quarter was the trough: ATM gross margin 21.2% against 29.2% a year earlier, ATM revenue down 20% year over year, utilization near 60%.
  • The EMS application rotation is only on one slide. Consumer share dropped 12 points in three quarters, from 40% (3Q25) to 28% (2Q26), while computing went 9% to 16% and industrial 12% to 16%.
  • Management's framing of its own advantage shifted from cost and scale to speed and architecture. The 2021 "4 Tailwinds" slides claim consolidation, Taiwan cluster efficiency and ASEH as "a de facto choice and indispensable manufacturing partner." The July 2026 slide claims "hardware infrastructure is bottleneck," "packaging is moving up in system architecture value chain," and an advantage built on "ecosystem position (cluster, scale, efficiency, pure-play, collaboration)" and "first mover's advantages." "Pure-play" is the only place in six years of decks where management distinguishes itself from a competitor type, and it does so without naming anyone.
  • What the decks do not contain. No competitor is named on any slide across 94 slides and six years; no customer is named and no concentration figure appears; no utilization figure appears despite utilization being the stated margin driver; no equipment counts; no technology roadmap, product slide or packaging-platform diagram, so FOCoS, FOCoS-Bridge, CoPoS and co-packaged optics appear nowhere; no cash flow statement, free cash flow, ROIC or returns disclosure of any kind; and no long-term financial target beyond a one-year LEAP dollar figure.

The 1Q26 and 2Q26 decks dropped the excluding-purchase-price-allocation block from the headline consolidated and ATM profit-and-loss slides, in the two quarters when reported margins were at record highs and the drag had become immaterial. And the ATM profit-and-loss slides use an ATM-basis revenue that includes intercompany revenue eliminated at the holding level, which the deck says only obliquely: 2Q26 ATM-basis total revenue is NT$126,148m against a consolidated ATM net revenue of NT$125,069m, and against NT$123,052m for packaging plus testing on §13.2's 6-K segment basis, a third figure for one quarter.

Appendix C — External data sources

One external dataset was identified for this company's archetype and is described below.

DRAM and NAND spot and contract pricing (mosaic) — memory_spot_pricing. What it is: a partial series of memory price points assembled from scattered dated and cited sources, because the comprehensive series (TrendForce) is paid. What it measures: the direction and magnitude of DRAM and NAND contract and spot price moves by quarter. How it would inform this analysis: memory pricing reaches ASE only indirectly, through two channels. The first is EMS revenue quality: management attributes the guided 40% sequential increase in 3Q26 EMS revenue largely to "component price hikes, particularly in the memory sector," confirms memory is "a pass-through type of cost," and states that ex-price-hikes the quarter's operating margin would be "around 3.7%, 3.8%" against a guided 3.2%–3.4%. A built series would bound how much of the FY2026 EMS revenue line is price rather than volume, which is the difference between a working-capital event and a demand recovery, and it would set the base for the 2027 comparison once the effect washes out. The second is HBM-adjacent packaging demand and the memory-customer volumes that sit inside ASE's mainstream wirebond and discrete lines. It would strengthen §6 (the secular-versus-cyclical split of the 2026 revenue acceleration) and the operational-KPI subsection of §13. Coverage and method: web mosaic, irregular cadence, no coded connector; assembled points would be medium-to-low confidence with explicit period gaps and would never be presented as a comprehensive series.
